html:
Unguldavor (Z52)

Survey region (English rating-table region): Escann.

In one sentence: Bring the Orc clans after the Greentide behind walls, into fields, and into cities in Escann, sustaining a new kingdom through cooperation rather than one conqueror.

Storytelling: High | Mission-tree length: Medium-long (39 direct Z52 missions) | Mission-tree update: based on the local script supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: High | Tedium: Medium (clan integration and urban construction) | Early pressure: determined by the predecessor | Expansion capacity: Medium-high

Not a starting kingdom

Unguldavor is not an established country selectable in 1444. The native Z52 history file contains only the post-formation government, culture, religion, and capital template; the normal formation decision requires a Green or Grey Orc to control at least ten cities in Inner Castanor, have Feudalism and Administrative technology level 7, and be at peace. Formation changes the country name and mission tree. The Severed Crown route has a separate script entry into Z52, so Unguldavor must not be described as exclusive to Clouded Eye. Clouded Eye’s Arosha story is important background and one route into the country, not a mandatory start for every campaign. [Local script]

The offline English Wiki describes Unguldavor as an Inner Castanor confederation of Orc clans founded by Arosha Oakbreaker, including Orcs and Half-Orcs and later associated with Corinite faith. This is Wiki worldbuilding; the game decision allows different qualifying Orc predecessors to form it, so Arosha’s founder story must not be applied automatically to every player campaign. [Wiki]

From walls to fields

The Z52 missions still begin with war, but their goal is not to continue the Greentide forever. The old White Wall defences must be repaired and the former Castanorian heartland farmed again. Mission text explicitly turns warriors “from swords to plowshares”, making escape from the Serpentspine and acquisition of a settled homeland the new national purpose. After controlling Inner Castanor, the capital and the tax, production, and administrative facilities of several clan cities become later thresholds; this is the practical operation of turning a mobile clan society into a settled kingdom, not only flavour text. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

The harder stage is power integration. The clan council tries to make different tribes cooperate, but council seats, cities, and old leaders’ interests keep raising the question of who represents the Orcs. Missions and events arrange the submission of clans, council construction, and vassal routes: the player must balance recognition of clan heritage with a governable central authority. Submission is not a single automatic outcome: different clans and routes can demand different political choices, and some solutions use coercion to force opponents to obey. Official Dev Diary 89 also frames this rework as a story of cooperation and rebuilding; success and the amount of coercion still depend on in-game decisions. [Local script] [Official Dev Diary]

This integration also appears in urban management. Flavour text mentions rebuilding old clan towns, courts after territorial rebellions, and academies for the children of chiefs, nobles, and wealthy families. It presents an Orc kingdom beginning to train administrators and send disputes to fixed institutions; the academy’s beneficiaries are clearly not the whole population, so it cannot establish equal education. Clans that once fought over land are required to live together beneath walls, fields, and a council, which is why this tree is slower and more distinctive than an ordinary conquest line. [Local narrative text]

Religion, alchemy, and the frontier

The country is not naturally of one opinion. Clouded Eye and Severed Ear are closer to Corinite justice and Orc–human equality, while other clans uphold Korgus’s strong tradition. The missions require the religious division to be handled and allow related faith directions; the player’s choice determines this campaign’s future, so universal conversion cannot be announced in the 1444 prehistory. The forest can support an independent alchemist’s laboratory, extending into early artificery and Serpentspine materials, giving the country a modernising Orc identity alongside its clan politics. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

Unguldavor’s “union” therefore does not erase every difference: clans bargain over faith, autonomy, and urban resources, and some routes use force to compel opponents. Outside battle, the player must continue investing in buildings and institutions so that the new frontier is more than an Orc colour on the map. Starting as Clouded Eye makes the personal leader and alchemical experiments a more continuous story; forming from another qualifying Orc still gives the Z52 tree, but Arosha’s every experience must not be treated as established history in that save. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

The most distinctive payoff is not one decisive victory, but seeing an old defensive line become the boundary of settled life, clan towns gain public facilities, and an alliance once held together by a chief’s prestige acquire institutions of its own. The missions promise stability that the player must build; it is not granted by the formation button. [Local script]

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 66/100 | Autocracy 58/100 | Magic↔Artifice 35/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 58/100) | Pluralism 79/100. The phase shift is scattered pre-formation clans (pluralism 44) → cooperation and urbanisation (pluralism 79).

The v2.1 values result is Good (71/100) with an improving trajectory. Repairing defences, farming, public urban construction, and cooperation across clans support public good and personhood; submission, religious conflict, and pre-formation war reduce restraint. Orc identity and kingdom formation do not change the score by themselves. Repairing walls, farming, urban governance, and cooperation across clans have clear public benefits; the submission and religious conflict reduce restraint. Different predecessors and religious choices can alter the picture, so confidence is medium.

This suits players who enjoy Escanni Orc state-building, post-war reconstruction, clan councils, and alchemical modernisation. If you only want uninterrupted Greentide-style conquest and do not want to wait for urban facilities or manage internal power, the second half will feel laborious. A 2026 player post particularly emphasises Clouded Eye’s alchemical and artificery potential; another is mainly an AI-formed-country map report. They show player experience only and do not define mission conditions. [Community views]

The exact scope of the local script, fixed Wiki revision, development diary, and two player posts is recorded in the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the idea set is adopted, the seven ideas unlock in sequence, and the ambition applies after all seven ideas. Only national ideas are listed; racial, government, and mission rewards are not mixed into the numbers. Formation ideas are not automatically stacked with the old set. Idea descriptions may recall history or describe a future ideal and do not automatically represent events already completed in 1444.

Unguldavor (Z52) — Unguldavori Ideas

Traditions: Unguldavori Traditions

Effects: Manpower recovery speed: +15%; Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 1: Wall of Forests

In the year 1494 AA, Arosha Oakbreaker founded our nation as a confederation of the clans of Clouded Eye, Bladebreaker, and Dogeater. She called this new realm Unguldavor -Wall of Forests. While an accurate description of our lands, it would take until the 1st Unguldavor War for the reason to become apparent.

The forces of Rosande, Hammerhome, and Marrhold invaded us with the intent of taking us as slaves. Had we been caught out in the lush fields of the south and west, we would have been conquered. However, our green skin and the dense forests gave us an advantage. Sneaking through the woods, we were able to ambush the knights of Rosande, render the diving griffons of Marrhold near-useless, and stall the dwarves. While we lost some territories, we were able to liberate the remnants of the Count’s League, which had been conquered earlier by Rosande.

Thus shall we never forget that Unguldavor makes us strong.

Effects: Fort defense: +20%

Idea 2: Land of Many Clans

At its founding, Unguldavor was not so much a nation as it was a confederation of several clans. Clouded Eye, Bladebreaker, Dogeater, and even remnants of Severed Ear, Bloodgorger, and many minor clans were all brought together under one banner. Arosha’s hope was to protect the orcs without destroying our traditions, and it was only under a strong ruler or invasion that the clans had historically rallied or cooperated.

Our society was fundamentally fractured. While Clouded Eye and Bladebreaker were Corinite, Bloodgorger and Dogeater were Dookanist. While Clouded Eye and Bloodgorger agreed on centralization, Severed Ear and Dogeater both wanted decentralization for different reasons. Some clans were eager to raid our neighbors, while others worked to repair the damage and establish an indigenous prosperity.

Although this ad hoc arrangement threatened to paralyze the state at a future date, it meant that constituent clans weren’t very rebellious and could send a decent army to Arosha’s court when the time arose to defend.

Effects: Liberty desire from subject development: -0.1; Vassal force limit contribution: +50%

Idea 3: King Grom the Great

Unguldavor was, for much of its early history, a chaotic land of rebellious clans with only nominal oversight. This would change under the reign of King Grom, who acceded to the throne in 1587. Taking control of Unguldavor after his older brother was overthrown by the Dookanist Revolt, Grom began by crushing the Dookanist Revolt and reviving Corinite fervor.

After dealing with the Dookanist Revolt, he launched the Great Submission of the Clans. He started by turning the clans against each other. With the clans distracted, he centralized the state in the urban centers, which were free of clan control, weakening their power. He struck an alliance with Corintar, legitimizing Unguldavor, making any attack on Unguldavor implicitly an attack on Corin’s legacy.

By 1617, King Grom the Great was finally ready to lead his first conquest, but old age caught up to him. Following his death and before his son’s coronation, the Shackle Kingdoms of Rosande, Covenblad, and Marrhold made a deal with Esthil in which the latter invaded Corintar so the former three could attack Unguldavor without Corintari intervention. This was the War of Treachery, which ended the era of Romantic Escann. However, Grom’s work wasn’t worthless: his work ensured there was an Unguldavor left.

Effects: Monarch diplomatic skill: +1

Idea 4: Legacy of Samûr

Over the first two decades of the seventeenth century, an Unguldavori alchemist named Samûr Ultanuhankar made himself known. He conducted several experiments, turning copper into gold and improving the strength of gunpowder. Much of his income came from specialty orders he received from rich clients, mixing potions to delay visible aging and give a boost of energy. He made a fortune and became a household name across Escann.

In 1618, his research focused on creating Halann’s first healing potion. He was working late into the night, already on a fiftieth attempt at mixing damestear and several other magical minerals into a serviceable base. The War of Treachery was in full swing, however, and it was not meant to be.

At dawn one winter morning, Rosande knights busted down the door, holding chains and marching ominously. They announced that he was to be enslaved and sent to labor as court alchemist for the “intellectually superior” king of Rosande and his council. Samûr, refusing to live a slave, grabbed a knife and fought back, but he was sixty summers old. He died in the lab, his blood staining his diagrams and notes. Rosande soldiers, not wanting the world to know what an orc was capable of, gathered up his documents and inventions before burning them, along with any literature and research paraphernalia they could find.

Effects: Innovativeness gain: +0.25; Artillery level contribution to siege: +50%

Idea 5: Twazabon Grall

After the War of Treachery, Unguldavor was a rump state, with most of its manpower enslaved and its knowledge destroyed. Confined to just Gulenhyl and the surrounding areas, it seemed inevitable that the polity would be annexed in short order. However, the War of the Black Tower brought about the application of Twazabon Grall - “the two-tongue speaker”. Twazabon Grall was a doctrine of diplomacy revolving around a pragmatic instead of ideological approach, emphasising alliances for the sake of national interest rather than from religious or principled motives.

As Esthili forces conquered Covenblad and Rosande, Unguldavor struck a secret alliance with Nurcestír. Under the terms of the alliance, Unguldavor would retake their lands currently occupied by Esthil while the larger Nurcestír army did most of the fighting. Unguldavor, in return, would become a vassal, receiving orcs from the rest of Escann.

When Camir began his march on Anbenncóst, the soul of Unguldavor survived, allowing it to be revived later when the Blackpowder Revolution overthrew Camiran rule.

Effects: Diplomatic reputation: +100% (inherited display; unit conversion unverified; script value: diplomatic_reputation = 1)

Idea 6: Riches of the Serpentspine

In the aftermath of the War of Treachery, Unguldavor survived by the skin of its teeth. There was not much hope to gain our lands back due to the Shackle Kingdoms of Rosande, Covenblad, and Marrhold, who maintained a firm alliance and diplomatically isolated us. In order to rebuild, we needed a new avenue of expansion, and the Serpentspine was the perfect candidate.

We traveled through the Clouded Wood to enter the caverns of the Serpentspine. What we found was a chaotic clash between tribes of dwarves, goblins, and kobolds. Using our warriors, we backed the kobolds to carve out a home for them. In return, they pledged allegiance and shipped to us mithril, serpentbloom, and all manners of goods unseen on the surface. In addition, we received manufactured goods from dwarven black market traders.

With the flow of mithril, we were able to make tools that last longer and are stronger. With mithril tools, we could finally make up for some of our lost production.

Effects: Goods produced modifier: +10%

Idea 7: Kabir Otabar

In the aftermath of the War of Treachery and collapse of Camiran Anbennar after around one hundred years as a vassal, the inevitable happened. Orcs were enslaved en masse now that Anbennarian control over Escann fell. Humans shipped off our brothers and sisters to Aelantir, stealing our land. It was in this environment that a new philosophy was born - Kabir Otabar, or ‘Great Fatherland’.

In 1775, Chief Churzan Bloodgorger gathered philosophers and shamans from across the country and first promulgated his doctrine. Under it, Kabir Otabar argued for a great orcish homeland for orcs, by orcs, and only for orcs. Humans had proven themselves deceitful weasels who would steal any land they could. At the same time, all orcs and half-orcs were brethren as long as they professed an allegiance to orckind and forsook any human aspects of their culture.

Kabir Otabar quickly spread to the Unguldavori court and in short order became state policy.

Effects: Culture conversion cost: -20%

Ambition: Unguldavori Ambition

Effects: Construction cost: -10%.
